tr: „I don't work on Monday.“
en: „I don't work on Monday.“

tr: „At half past six. Don't be late!“
en: „At half past six. Don't be late!“

tr: Saati yaz. Sonunda günlük programı doldur.
en: Write the time. At the end, fill in the daily plan.

tr: „Rice with vegetables. It's easy and cheap.“
en: „Rice with vegetables. It's easy and cheap.“

tr: Hesap ödeniyor. Nakit mi, kart mı, birlikte mi?
en: The bill is being paid. Cash, card or together?

tr: „I often work on Saturday morning.“ — akşamları boş.
en: „I often work on Saturday morning.“ — in the evening she is free.

tr: „No, thank you. Beer is enough.“ — şarabı reddediyor.
en: „No, thank you. Beer is enough.“ — he turns the wine down.

tr: „Eight euros together, then.“ — üç artı dört artı bir.
en: „Eight euros together, then.“ — three plus four plus one.

tr: Üç kişi içecek söylüyor. Kim ne alıyor, toplam kaç para?
en: Three people order drinks. Who takes what, how much is it all together?

tr: „First … after that … finally“ üç adımı sırayla bağlıyor.
en: „First … after that … finally“ links the three steps in order.

tr: „On Sunday I usually cook.“ — ona kadar uyumak cumartesi.
en: „On Sunday I usually cook.“ — sleeping until ten belongs to Saturday.

tr: Önce davet, sonra özür, sonra soru, en son başlama saati.
en: First the invitation, then the apology, then the question, last the starting time.

tr: „I don't work on Sunday.“ — gün adından önce „on“ geliyor.
en: „I don't work on Sunday.“ — „on“ comes before the name of a day.

tr: „It's a quarter to nine.“ — dokuza çeyrek kala, yani 8:45.
en: „It's a quarter to nine.“ — a quarter before nine, that is 8:45.

tr: Ela pazar alışverişini anlatıyor. Ne aldı, ne kadar ödedi?
en: Ela talks about her shopping at the market. What did she buy, what did she pay?

tr: „The beer is four euros“ — üç euro meyve suyu, bir euro su.
en: „The beer is four euros“ — three euros is the juice, one euro the water.

tr: Önce pazara gidiş, sonra sipariş, sonra fiyat, en son ödeme.
en: First going to the market, then the order, then the price, last the payment.

tr: „I usually wake up at seven, but today my clock doesn't work.“
en: „I usually wake up at seven, but today my clock doesn't work.“

tr: „I usually walk to work.“ — üçüncü tekil kişide „-s“: he walks.
en: „I usually walk to work.“ — in the third person singular a „-s“: he walks.

tr: „I'd like a juice… Apple, please.“ — bira Kaan'ın, su Deniz'in.
en: „I'd like a juice… Apple, please.“ — the beer is Kaan's, the water is Deniz's.

tr: „Tomatoes are cheap this week — it's a sale.“ — pahalı olan et.
en: „Tomatoes are cheap this week — it's a sale.“ — the expensive one is the meat.

tr: „Never! I work from Monday to Friday.“ — hafta sonu çalışan Nil.
en: „Never! I work from Monday to Friday.“ — the one who works at the weekend is Nil.

tr: Bir günün tamamı saatleriyle anlatılıyor. Hangi iş hangi saatte?
en: A whole day is told with its times. What happens when?

tr: Tarif yaz. Emir kipinde özne yazılmıyor, fiil doğrudan başlıyor.
en: Write a recipe. The imperative has no subject, the sentence starts with the verb.

tr: „Then we close in one hour, at ten.“ — bir saat sonra, yani onda.
en: „Then we close in one hour, at ten.“ — in one hour, that is at ten.

tr: „Two euros a kilo.“ — yarım euro muzun fiyatı, dokuz euro toplam.
en: „Two euros a kilo.“ — half a euro is the price of a banana, nine euros the total.

tr: Bir haftanın düzeni. Hangi iş her zaman, hangisi bazen yapılıyor?
en: The shape of one week. What happens always, what only sometimes?

tr: „First, I wake up at six.“ — kalkmak ikinci adım, kahvaltı üçüncü.
en: „First, I wake up at six.“ — getting up is the second step, breakfast the third.

tr: İki kişi birlikte yemek pişiriyor. Hangi adım önce, hangisi sonra?
en: Two people cook together. Which step comes first, which comes after?

tr: „Here is the bill. Twenty-four euros, please.“ — on, kapanış saati.
en: „Here is the bill. Twenty-four euros, please.“ — ten is the closing time.

tr: „It's half past eight.“ — „half past“ dokuzun değil sekizin buçuğu.
en: „It's half past eight.“ — „half past“ counts from the hour that has gone, so it is half an hour after eight.

tr: Saatler ve günlük akış. „past“ geçe, „to“ kala — ikisine de dikkat.
en: Times and a daily routine. „past“ means after, „to“ means before — watch both.

tr: Sabahın adımları sırayla. First, then, after that, before, finally.
en: The steps of a morning in order. First, then, after that, before, finally.

tr: „Yes, it's very hot. Don't touch it!“ — ılık olan çay, su çok sıcak.
en: „Yes, it's very hot. Don't touch it!“ — the tea is warm, the water is very hot.

tr: Hafta sonu ne yapılıyor? Sıklık zarflarını ve gün edatlarını yakala.
en: What happens at the weekend? Catch the adverbs of frequency and the prepositions of days.

tr: Önce Ela, sonra Kaan, sonra Deniz söylüyor; toplam en sonda çıkıyor.
en: First Ela orders, then Kaan, then Deniz; the total comes last.

tr: „I work from nine until five.“ — „from … until …“ başlangıç ve bitiş.
en: „I work from nine until five.“ — „from … until …“ gives a start and an end.

tr: „I prefer tea to coffee.“ — tercih edilen önce, ötekisi „to“dan sonra.
en: „I prefer tea to coffee.“ — what is preferred comes first, the other after „to“.

tr: Biri sevdiği ve sevmediği yemekleri anlatıyor. Kim neyi tercih ediyor?
en: Someone talks about the food they love and the food they hate. Who prefers what?

tr: „First, wash the rice.“ — emir kipinde özne yok, fiil doğrudan geliyor.
en: „First, wash the rice.“ — the imperative has no subject, the verb comes straight away.

tr: „In the evening I turn off the radio.“ — sabah açıyor, akşam kapatıyor.
en: „In the evening I turn off the radio.“ — he turns it on in the morning and off in the evening.

tr: „It's half past eight.“ — sekiz buçuk; on bir çeyrek Nil'in uyku saati.
en: „It's half past eight.“ — half an hour after eight; a quarter past eleven is when Nil sleeps.

tr: „The meat is expensive: nine euros a kilo.“ İndirimde daha ucuz oluyor.
en: „The meat is expensive: nine euros a kilo.“ In a sale it gets cheaper.

tr: „At the end I pay by card.“ — ödeme biçimi „by“ ile: by card, by cheque.
en: „At the end I pay by card.“ — the way of paying takes „by“: by card, by cheque.

tr: „I don't work on Monday. I wake up at nine…“ — yedi Can'ın kalkma saati.
en: „I don't work on Monday. I wake up at nine…“ — seven is when Can gets up.

tr: „I usually walk to work.“ — „usually“ „always“ değil; her zaman demiyor.
en: „I usually walk to work.“ — „usually“ is not „always“; it does not mean every time.

tr: Sıklık zarfının yeri kurala bağlı: ana fiilden ÖNCE, „be“ fiilinden SONRA.
en: The place of the frequency adverb follows a rule: BEFORE the main verb, AFTER the verb „be“.

tr: „…I look for my keys.“ — „look for“ aramak demek; „look“ tek başına bakmak.
en: „…I look for my keys.“ — „look for“ means to search; „look“ on its own means to see.

tr: „I always drink tea, never coffee.“ — iki zarf aynı cümlede karşıt duruyor.
en: „I always drink tea, never coffee.“ — two adverbs stand against each other in one sentence.

tr: Pazarda pazarlık. Kilo, gram ve fiyat art arda geliyor — sayıları takip et.
en: Bargaining at the market. Kilos, grams and prices come one after the other — follow the numbers.

tr: „I hate cutting onions.“ — „hate“ fiilinden sonra ikinci fiil „-ing“ alıyor.
en: „I hate cutting onions.“ — after „hate“ the second verb takes „-ing“.

tr: „Nine euros! That's too expensive for me.“ — daha az alınca beş euro oluyor.
en: „Nine euros! That's too expensive for me.“ — with less it comes to five euros.

tr: Ödeme ve alışveriş isteklerini yaz. Sayılabilen çoğulda „are“, tekilde „is“.
en: Write requests for paying and shopping. A countable plural takes „are“, a singular takes „is“.

tr: „We begin at half past nine.“ — çeyrek geçe şimdiki saat, yani Ali geç değil.
en: „We begin at half past nine.“ — a quarter past is the time now, so Ali is not late.

tr: „I usually wake up at seven“ — „wake up“ iki parçalı bir fiil, parçası düşmez.
en: „I usually wake up at seven“ — „wake up“ is a two-part verb and no part may be dropped.

tr: „Before work, I turn off the TV.“ — açmak sabahın başında, kapatmak işten önce.
en: „Before work, I turn off the TV.“ — it goes on at the start of the morning and off before work.

tr: „Four euros. Tomatoes are cheap this week.“ — dokuz ve beş euro etin fiyatları.
en: „Four euros. Tomatoes are cheap this week.“ — nine and five euros are the prices of the meat.

tr: „I don't like sweet food — I hate very sweet cakes!“ — „hate“ en güçlü olumsuz.
en: „I don't like sweet food — I hate very sweet cakes!“ — „hate“ is the strongest refusal.

tr: Önce hesap gelir, sonra birlikte ödeme sorulur, sonra ödeme biçimi, en son saat.
en: First the bill comes, then the question about paying together, then the way of paying, last the time.

tr: „First, wash the rice. Then cut the onions.“ — soğan ikinci, domates üçüncü adım.
en: „First, wash the rice. Then cut the onions.“ — the onion is the second step, the tomato the third.

tr: „I always drink tea, never coffee.“ — sıklık zarfı ana fiilden önce: always drink.
en: „I always drink tea, never coffee.“ — the frequency adverb comes before the main verb: always drink.

tr: „I'd like to pay by card… I only have a card too.“ Çek, Eda'nın işi için bir belge.
en: „I'd like to pay by card… I only have a card too.“ The cheque is a record for Eda's work.

tr: „After work I buy fruit and vegetables at the market.“ — ekmek ve peynir kahvaltıda.
en: „After work I buy fruit and vegetables at the market.“ — bread and cheese belong to breakfast.

tr: „Here you are. Eleven euros, please.“ — dört euro domates, beş euro et, iki euro su.
en: „Here you are. Eleven euros, please.“ — four euros of tomatoes, five of meat, two of water.

tr: „Sometimes I am late, but my teacher is never angry.“ — „never“ „be“ fiilinden SONRA.
en: „Sometimes I am late, but my teacher is never angry.“ — „never“ comes AFTER the verb „be“.

tr: „Then look for a new clock at the weekend!“ — Ali de „On Saturday I have time“ diyor.
en: „Then look for a new clock at the weekend!“ — Ali agrees with „On Saturday I have time“.

tr: „I have dinner at half past seven.“ — „half past seven“ yedi buçuk, sekiz buçuk değil.
en: „I have dinner at half past seven.“ — „half past seven“ is half an hour after seven, not after eight.

tr: „I always get up at seven, also at the weekend.“ — „also“ hafta sonunu da içine alıyor.
en: „I always get up at seven, also at the weekend.“ — „also“ takes the weekend in as well.

tr: „I always turn it off before I sleep.“ — nesne zamir olunca ARAYA giriyor: turn it off.
en: „I always turn it off before I sleep.“ — when the object is a pronoun it goes IN BETWEEN: turn it off.

tr: Zaman edatlarını yaz: günde „on“, hafta sonunda „at“, sabahta „in“. Üçü üç ayrı sözcük.
en: Write the prepositions of time: „on“ with a day, „at“ with the weekend, „in“ with the morning. Three cases, three different words.

tr: „The food I love most is pizza with meat and onion.“ — pirinci kız kardeş tercih ediyor.
en: „The food I love most is pizza with meat and onion.“ — the rice is what the sister prefers.

tr: „I wake up at six and I get up at a quarter past six.“ — uyanmak ile kalkmak ayrı iki iş.
en: „I wake up at six and I get up at a quarter past six.“ — waking up and getting up are two different things.

tr: Önce miktar, sonra sipariş, sonra itiraz, en son toplam. Pazarlık hep bu sırayla gidiyor.
en: First the amount, then the order, then the objection, last the total. Bargaining always runs in this order.

tr: Sevdiğini ve tercih ettiğini yaz. Dikkat: sevmek fiilinden sonra ikinci fiil „-ing“ alıyor.
en: Write what you like and what you prefer. Careful: after a verb of liking the second verb takes „-ing“.

tr: Geç kalan bir öğrenci. Phrasal verb'lerin hepsi bir arada: come in, sit down, turn on, look for.
en: A student who is late. All the phrasal verbs at once: come in, sit down, turn on, look for.
